title: TT-Bio benchmarks: biomolecular structure prediction, design and binding affinity on Tenstorrent hardware
subtitle: Eight structure-prediction models, two binder-design models and one binding-affinity model at 512 residues, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200, B200 and A100.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

A row is published only when every processor column is measured. A model with a blank column waits in perf/page_rows_pending.json until its missing cells exist, because a half-measured row still draws a bar and reads as a claim. scripts/site_publish_guard.py enforces this, --strip holds a row and --restore publishes it.

One cell per model per platform. A Tenstorrent cell is tt-bio main in its default mode, with its --fast run kept beside it under `fast`; an NVIDIA cell is the Anthropic kit's exact mode where the kit has the model (ref "kit") and the authors' own release where it does not (ref "stock"), with the other runs kept as `fast` and `stock`. Every Tenstorrent cell states its accuracy from the release gate (perf/bmk/gate_parity.py). Numbers come from state/bmk/BOARD.md through perf/bmk/board_to_page.py. A cell with no measurement gets a status and a reason, never an estimate.

The A100 appears twice: as a card, and as the DGX A100 640GB, the eight-GPU box NVIDIA sold that card in. The $175,000 that box carries is an assumed street price, not a vendor list price, and it is labelled as one everywhere it is used.
A design model carrying 'hidden': true keeps every measured cell here and is drawn nowhere. Delete that one line to publish the row again.

Every Tenstorrent cell states the board it was measured on. It inherits `measured_on` from its platform and overrides it only if it ran somewhere else. The column is priced as a p150a; the board that produced the number is a separate fact and is stated as one.

The embed block is measured but not published. All six rows carry "hidden": true and the page has no code that reads it, so the guard counts them out of the title, the subtitle and the meta description. site/README.md records what was run. Restoring the section means dropping the flags, putting the chart and the t-embed table back, and moving EXPECT_ROWS.embed in render_check.js in the same commit.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm runs, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same two input files on every platform, each model at its own shipped recycle and sampling-step settings. Each Tenstorrent cell is tt-bio main in its default mode.
scope.nvidia_code: An NVIDIA cell is one of two things, and the page says which for every cell. Where Anthropic's open kit for these models (github.com/anthropics/uplifting-biomolecular-modeling, commit f4f62fa65) carries the model, it is the kit in its exact mode: the authors' upstream package, patched in memory with fused kernels and CUDA graphs that keep its arithmetic. Otherwise it is the authors' own release with nothing added. Neither is NVIDIA BioNeMo or a NIM. Each kit cell's machine also timed the kit's fast mode, which gives up bit-for-bit agreement for speed, and the unpatched upstream package; both are in the hover text and the data file, not on the bars.
scope.nvidia_impl: Exact mode was checked rather than assumed. On the A100, with determinism switched on, OpenFold3, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE returned the same coordinates as the unpatched package bit for bit, and ESMC the same pooled embeddings. Boltz-2 was not run that way, and the kit runs OpenBind-0 from a bf16 configuration where upstream ships fp32; for both, the median distance between the kit's structure and the unpatched package's is smaller than the median distance between two runs of the unpatched package.
scope.gpu_generations: The B200 is not uniformly faster than the H200 on these workloads. Six rows go the H200's way by a clear margin: Boltz-2 by 10.2 %, OpenFold3 15.9 %, OpenBind-0 16.0 %, BoltzGen 27.2 %, ESMFold2-Fast 78.3 % and Nesso-1 84.0 %. PXDesign is the one row where the two are level, 0.7 % to the H200 against within-arm spreads of 5.1 % and 5.5 %. Every other row goes the B200's way. The B200 cells were re-measured on a config-identical machine and reproduce within 4.1 %, so the split is real. It is not the host: cutting the B200 box from 24 cores to 6 with taskset moves Boltz-2 by less than 1.5 % (8.285 / 8.163 / 8.192 s), and on single-threaded featurisation the B200 box's Xeon 8559C is 1.51x faster than the H200 box's Xeon 8480+ (8.275 s against 12.459 s on the same RoseTTAFold3 work), so the host difference runs toward the B200, not against it. The mechanism is saturation. Solving Boltz-2 at four recycle and sampling-step points on both cards gives 0.541 s per recycle on the B200 against 0.620 s on the H200, and 0.0288 s per sampling step against 0.0241 s: the B200 is the faster trunk, the H200 is the faster sampler. The published Boltz-2 cell is 70 % sampler on the B200 and 66 % on the H200, and the sampler phase draws 379 W of the B200's 1000 W limit at 68 % utilisation against 404 W of the H200's 700 W at 90 %. At 512 residues these workloads do not fill a B200. One packaging term was measured and it is small: cuEquivariance's Blackwell triangle-attention kernel ships only in the cu13 wheels and the published cells ran cu12; per call it is 2.69x faster, end to end it moves Boltz-2 by -2.76 % and BoltzGen the wrong way by +4.28 %.
scope.timed_region: Each cell times what that platform's own harness times, and the regions are not identical: every Tenstorrent number is a whole prediction call with featurisation and structure writing inside it, and on NVIDIA that is true of RoseTTAFold3 and effectively true of ESMFold2, but the Boltz-2, OpenFold3, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE cells time the network forward and leave host work outside the timer. What they leave out is 0.24 s, 0.43 s, 0.62 s and 6.31 s per prediction, which makes those four ratios larger than a like-for-like comparison would.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is this page's assumption for how long an AI accelerator earns its keep: one year shorter than the general-purpose server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q, because an accelerator generation lasts about two years. A shorter window favours the cheaper box, so the range below brackets it.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Throughput per dollar, with the DGX H200 set to 1.00x, on two bases. Purchase price: predictions per hour / price, with no amortisation window, because the window cancels from that ratio. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour / cost per hour, where cost per hour = price / (4 x 8766 h) + power kW x $/kWh.
cost_model.sensitivity: Shift the window to 3 or 6 years, or the rate to the 13.54 c/kWh US commercial tariff, and the Tenstorrent figure moves between 2.47x and 3.71x. It does not invert.

models.note: At 16.6 seq/s this row is slower than SaProt 1.3B at 23.4 on the same card, which reads as a page bug and is not one. SaProt 35M has a head dim of 24 (hidden 480 over 20 heads), neither tile-aligned nor aligned with the fused on-device rotary kernel, so the port splits heads, applies RoPE on host in fp32 and pads 24 to 32 on host, once per layer. That costs 35.2 ms per layer against 4.5-4.7 ms per layer for the two larger sizes at hidden 1280, and it is also why this is the widest-spread Tenstorrent row here at 13.0 %. Documented in docs/saprot-parity.md under "35M host-side RoPE path"; a fix is proposed, not landed.

NVIDIA does not post DGX pricing and published no list price for this system, and no vendor quote is cited for it, so it is the one price here that is not a published figure. Every DGX A100 cost bar rests on it.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware. BoltzGen returns a binder design, not a prediction; its bars share an axis with the prediction models but not a unit.

The A100 ran every cell on this page, on the same fixtures. Its host is an AMD EPYC 7513 where the H200 and B200 boxes were Intel Xeon, which matters for the dispatch-bound trunks and is not corrected for, and the RoseTTAFold3 cell ran later on an EPYC 7763 at the same 30.7 vCPU quota. PXDesign's A100 cell is a third box, an EPYC 7713 at a 30.72 vCPU quota, picked to hold that quota because 3.1 s of its number is host featurisation.

RoseTTAFold3's NVIDIA cells carry the widest spreads on this page, and host featurisation is why: host prep varies far more run to run than device work does, so raising the H200 cell from three folds to eight moved its median 3.6 % and left the spread where it was.

PXDesign's NVIDIA cells are the only ones on this page measured on torch 2.7.1 with CUDA 12.8; every other row's NVIDIA cells are torch 2.3.1 on CUDA 12.1. PXDesign needed the move because CUDA 12.1 emits no sm_100 device code, so its B200 could not otherwise run what its H200 measured, and a row is only worth reading if all of it comes from one stack. Within the PXDesign row the three NVIDIA cells are on that one stack. Across rows they are not, which is another reason caveat 1 applies: compare a model to itself.
